ABN AMRO Clearing (AAC) is a leading global player in clearing and clearing related services and strives to optimize profitability, return on invested capital and shareholders value. We have offices around the world, operating in Sydney since 1998; other main offices are located in Hong Kong, Tokyo, Singapore, Amsterdam, London, Chicago and Brazil. AAC is ambitious and customer oriented, striving to provide the best integrated service package for the professional business. AAC is a reliable partner, with efficient operations, compliant to all regulations and with a sound risk framework. 

The Software Engineer role contributes to AAC’s mission to optimize performance, risk management, and operational excellence by designing, developing, and maintaining enterprise software systems. The position ensures that applications are scalable, reliable, and compliant with financial regulations across APAC. 

The Software Engineer will report to the RAMS APAC Product Owner and be responsible for end-to-end design, development, migration, and optimization of critical clearing applications. This includes: 
• Designing system architecture for applications across Linux, Windows, PostgreSQL, MS SQL, and DB2 environments. 
• Leading upgrades and migrations of legacy applications to modern frameworks (Java, Angular, Python, Perl). 
• Ensuring integration, scalability, performance, and maintainability across APAC platforms. 

Key Responsibilities:
1. Software System Design & Architecture 
o Design and implement robust, scalable software architectures for LCM applications. 
o Evaluate and select frameworks, tools, and technologies to optimize system performance. 
o Define database structures and interactions to support enterprise systems. 
2. Development & Engineering 
o Develop, test, and maintain software solutions in Java, Python, Perl, and Angular, aligned with architectural design. 
o Apply engineering best practices (Spring MVC, Spring Boot, Maven, Bootstrap CSS) to ensure maintainable and high-quality code. 
3. Application Lifecycle Management 
o Own the full software lifecycle, including design, coding, testing, deployment, and support. 
o Lead migration projects, upgrading legacy systems to modern platforms while maintaining system integrity. 
4. Technical Leadership & Advisory 
o Provide guidance to Product Owners and the RAMS team on system design, technical decisions, and software strategy. 
o Evaluate software solutions for cost, risk, scalability, and integration into existing APAC systems. 
5. Collaboration & Documentation 
o Work closely with IT teams, Chapter Leads, and APAC CIO to maintain alignment between business needs and software architecture. 
o Produce and maintain technical documentation, including architecture diagrams, operational procedures, and user manuals. 
6. Risk & Compliance Awareness 
o Ensure all system designs meet regulatory, security, and operational risk requirements. 
o Implement solutions to improve reliability, compliance, and performance of critical clearing systems. 

Required Knowledge and Experience Education: 
• IT-related university degree or equivalent. 
• At least 2+ years in software engineering or system architecture roles. 
• Experience in finance/clearing systems preferred. 

Technical Skills: 
• Software engineering and system architecture experience. 
• Programming: Java (mandatory), Python/Perl, Angular. 
• Frameworks: Spring MVC, Spring Boot, Maven, Bootstrap CSS. 
• Databases: PostgreSQL, MS SQL, DB2, including design and optimization. 
• Operating Systems: Linux, Windows, Unix. 
• Lifecycle management, software engineering methodologies, test management, and IT governance.

Job no: 944478

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide CBD

Categories: Information-Communication Technology, Public Health, Research and Data Analysis




 

The Commission on Excellence and Innovation in Health (CEIH) - Clinical Informatics and Innovation Directorate (CIID) - SACCaN D&I (South Australian Comprehensive Cancer Network Data and Intelligence)

Salary: $130,046 to $134,956 - ASO8 - Full Time - Term Contract up to 12 Months

Overview:

The Data Architect provides strategic leadership in the design, development and governance of a complex, patient-centric enterprise data architecture, including a data lakehouse, multiple analytical platforms, and associated data integration and interoperability requirements. The role ensures that high-value clinical, operational and research data assets are usable, trusted, secure and fit for purpose to support the objectives of the SA Cancer Network.

The Data Architect interprets complex business, clinical and information requirements and translates them into conceptual, logical, and physical data architectures, data models and standards. Working collaboratively with clinicians, the CEIH Clinical Informatics and Innovation Directorate (CIID), solution architects and other stakeholders, the role ensures a consistent, interoperable, and standards-based approach to data design across systems, platforms and agencies.

The role leads the definition, implementation and continuous improvement of data architecture frameworks, standards, patterns, and best practices, including lakehouse design, data modelling, metadata management, master and reference data, and data integration approaches. The Data Architect provides architectural assurance to ensure data solutions align with enterprise architecture, agreed Digital Health and CIID standards, and whole-of-government data and digital strategies.

The Data Architect works collaboratively with delivery teams, customers, and stakeholders to understand data and information needs, providing authoritative technical consultancy and design guidance to inform solution options, platform adoption and investment decisions. The role ensures that data architectures enable advanced analytics, reporting, research, and insight generation as well as supporting patient-centric care models.

The CIID values innovation, excellence, collaboration, knowledge sharing, transparency, accountability, and respect.

The Commission on Excellence and Innovation in Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

Job ref: 944478

A 'National Police Certificate' NPC (also known as a 'Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check' NCCHC) for employment involving no contact with vulnerable groups is required for this position (general employment).

A DHS 'Working With Children Check' (WWCC) is required for this position.

Immunisation Risk for this position is Category C (minimal patient contact).

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Design Documentation and Drafting

About the Business:
Final Touch Joinery Pty Ltd is a reputable North-West Sydney-based cabinetry specialist established in 2006 by Director Nathan Diab. With a strong commitment to quality craftsmanship and exceptional customer service, the company specialises in custom kitchen joinery, wardrobes, vanities, and architectural fit-outs for both residential and commercial clients, including high-end homes, unit developments, pubs, clubs, and insurance repair projects. Using premium materials and advanced CAD software, Final Touch Joinery delivers tailored solutions that bring clients’ visions to life with precision, durability, and elegant finishes. The business prides itself on a collaborative, detail-oriented workplace culture where innovation meets traditional joinery skills in a supportive environment focused on excellence and client satisfaction.
About the Position:
The Cabinet Maker plays a vital role in fabricating, assembling, and installing high-quality custom cabinetry, kitchens, wardrobes, and other joinery solutions for Final Touch Joinery’s diverse residential and commercial projects. Working from detailed drawings and client specifications, this position contributes directly to creating functional, beautiful spaces that meet the highest standards of finish and craftsmanship, helping the company maintain its reputation for premium, personalised results in the joinery industry.
Key Responsibilities:
Examining drawings, work orders, and sample parts to determine specifications.
Selecting and working with materials such as timber, veneers, particle board, laminates, and other engineered wood products.
Marking out, cutting, shaping, and assembling components using hand tools, power tools, and computer numerical control (CNC) machines where applicable.
Fabricating and installing kitchen, bathroom, and other cabinetry, wardrobes, counters, and fittings.
Fitting hinges, locks, catches, drawers, shelves, and other hardware with precision.
Ensuring all work meets quality standards, safety requirements, and client expectations.
Collaborating with the team on commercial and residential fit-outs, including repairs and custom solutions.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Minimum Certificate III in Cabinet Making and Installation, Joinery, or any relevant field or at least 2 years of relevant experience.
Minimum 2 years of experience as a cabinet maker or in a related field.
Strong technical skills in reading technical drawings, precise measurement, woodworking machinery operation, and use of hand/power tools.
Excellent attention to detail, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to quality craftsmanship.
Good interpersonal and communication skills to collaborate effectively with team members and understand client requirements.
Physical fitness and ability to work safely in a workshop and on-site environment.

To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 


We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 


As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 


Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.






Enterprise Architect




Care, reimagined


Design and deliver innovative learning that builds clinical digital capability


Permanent, full time role, hybrid workplace model




Make a Difference Through Digital Health.




Great healthcare technology isn't defined by the systems we buy-it's defined by how well those systems work together to support care. This pivotal role is about shaping the future digital landscape of Monash Health, connecting strategy, architecture and innovation to ensure every technology investment delivers meaningful value. As Enterprise Architect, you'll provide the architectural vision and governance that enables smarter decisions, reduces complexity and creates a more connected, sustainable and future-ready health service.





About The Role



We are now seeking an experienced and passionate Enterprise Architect to join our Design & Architecture Services team within the Digital and Information Division.



As Enterprise Architect, you will provide strategic architectural leadership across Monash Health's technology landscape, helping shape the future direction of digital investment and technology-enabled care. You will assess current capabilities, identify opportunities to simplify and rationalise the application portfolio, and ensure new technology investments align with organisational strategy, architectural standards and long-term sustainability goals. Acting as a trusted advisor to executives and technical leaders alike, you will play a critical role in defining the future-state architecture that supports Monash Health's ongoing transformation. 




What We're Looking For



You are a strategic thinker and trusted advisor who can see the bigger picture while translating complex technology landscapes into clear, practical direction. You bring significant experience in enterprise architecture, technology strategy and digital transformation within large, complex organisations, with the ability to align technology investments to long-term organisational objectives.



Highly analytical and solutions-focused, you enjoy solving complex challenges, managing technical debt and identifying opportunities to modernise systems, improve interoperability and strengthen organisational capability. You understand the importance of balancing innovation with governance, security, risk management and regulatory compliance.



You'll Also Bring:





Significant experience in enterprise architecture, technology strategy and digital transformation.


Expertise in architecture frameworks, governance and target-state planning.


Ability to evaluate technology investments and assess strategic fit across a complex environment.


Strong communication skills with the ability to influence executive and technical audiences.


Experience simplifying complex technology landscapes and driving architectural maturity.






Experience in healthcare or digital health is highly regarded.




Why join Monash Health?



This is more than a digital role-it's your chance to transform healthcare at scale. Working at the intersection of clinical care, technology and innovation, you'll help create smarter digital solutions that improve patient outcomes and support the clinicians who deliver them every day




At Monash Health, you will:



Lead a state-wide service with real impact


Work within a values-driven, purpose-led organisation


Be part of a connected network of clinical, academic and system leaders


Help drive innovation, inclusion and better health outcomes





We also offer:



The opportunity to make a real impact on patient experience


A supportive, collaborative team environment


Ongoing learning and development opportunities


The chance to be part of Victoria's largest public health service





For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Robert Dashwood by email- Robert.Dashwoodo@monashhealth.org



To view the Position Description, click the link below




#8766 Enterprise Architect-Position Description.pdf







Our Culture and Values 



At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 



Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 



You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 




We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 



We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 




If you're passionate about helping clinicians embrace digital innovation and want to influence the future of healthcare at scale, we'd love to hear from you.

Custom Clad is a specialist façade and cladding subcontractor delivering architectural building envelope solutions across commercial, residential and institutional projects. We are seeking a full-time Structural Engineer (ANZSCO 233214) to join our engineering team.

Key tasks and duties

Determine the structural design methods and materials to be used in façade, cladding and framing systems, and provide specifications for their construction.
Prepare and interpret engineering sketches, drawings, plans and specifications for building envelope elements and support structures.
Analyse and assess the behaviour of structural systems and components under load, including wind, dead and live loading, to ensure structural integrity and compliance with the National Construction Code and relevant Australian Standards.
Perform structural calculations and design checks for cladding substrates, subframes, brackets and fixings, and provide certification input where required.
Provide technical advice on structural and engineering matters to project managers, estimators, site teams and clients.
Coordinate with architects, builders, building surveyors and consultants to resolve design and buildability issues.
Conduct site inspections and investigate structural failures or defects, and prepare reports on findings and remedial recommendations.

Ensure engineering work complies with Australian Standards, workplace health and safety requirements and quality assurance procedures.

Positive skills assessment from Engineers Australia (or eligibility to obtain one).
Sound knowledge of the National Construction Code and relevant Australian Standards, including AS/NZS 1170 and AS 4100.
Proficiency in structural analysis and design software and AutoCAD or Revit.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary project team.

result.description:
Plumber – Greystanes NSW

Kogan People Solutions, recruiters, are working with an innovative and well-regarded plumbing business operating across NSW. The company delivers high-quality commercial and residential plumbing services, including new installations, maintenance, upgrades, and repairs. With a strong reputation for reliability, modern practices, and exceptional customer service, our client is seeking an experienced and qualified Plumber to support continued growth and service delivery.

About the Role

The Plumber will work across commercial and residential sites, performing installation, maintenance, fault-finding, and repair work. The successful candidate will work closely with clients, contractors, and internal teams to ensure all plumbing work is completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with NSW regulatory requirements.

•	Tenure: Full time & Ongoing

•	Location (base): Greystanes, NSW

•	Salary: Negotiable in the range $80,000 to $90,000 plus superannuation per annum  

Responsibilities will include:

•	Install, maintain, and repair plumbing systems, fixtures, pipes, and associated equipment in line with the Plumbing Code of Australia (PCA) and AS/NZS 3500.

•	Complete comprehensive plumbing work for residential and commercial new builds, renovations, fit-outs, and system upgrades.

•	Diagnose complex faults, clear blockages, isolate leaks, and carry out corrective repairs.

•	Read and interpret plans, architectural blueprints, technical specifications, and compliance documentation.

•	Liaise with clients, contractors, and internal stakeholders to ensure smooth project delivery.

•	Ensure all work complies with NSW plumbing, drainage, and gas fitting safety regulations.

•	Maintain accurate job records, reports, and compliance documentation, including contributing to Certificates of Compliance (CoC).

•	Contribute to continuous improvement and uphold high industry service standards.

To be successfully considered for this role you will:

 *  Be qualified to Certificate IV level or agreed equivalent 

 *  Hold,  or be eligible to acquire, all relevant certificates enabling employment in NSW.

 *  Have at least one or more  years of relevant plumbing experience in residential or commercial settings (incorporating new installations, maintenance, and repairs).

 *  Possess strong technical skills across water supply, sanitary plumbing, drainage, and general plumbing systems.

 *  Hold, or be eligible to acquire, a  General Construction Induction Card (White Card).

*   Possess a valid Australian Driver’s Licence.

 *  Demonstrate strong communication, customer service, and independent task-management skills.

 *  Provide solid professional references upon request.

Desirable Requirements:

•	Verification of Competency (VOC) or Statement of Attainment (SOA) excavator ticket.

•	Confined Spaces Rescuer certification (Sydney Water Procedure - WHSMS0068).

•	Work Safely at Heights certification.

•	First Aid certification.

•	Demonstrated experience working with Sydney Water safety protocols and procedures.

Applications

Please respond to the recruiters using the facilities on this site, and ensure you attach your updated CV.

Kogan People Solutions are grateful for all applications, but kindly note that they will only respond to shortlisted applicants.
